frontier.hypothesis: The function closes on the h1/giv chassis (which already has target's preheader; its whole residual is the i/p-walker swap) as soon as a post-loop reuse demotes the counter's allocno priority below the giv's 9310 - and the reuse must have TWO joining definitions, since adjacent def/use pairs are copy-propagated away and a plain post-loop READ of `i` is constant-folded (loop.c knows i == 2).
frontier.mechanism: pri = floor_log2(refs)*refs/live_length with cc1's own numbers. Requirement table (session 7, unchanged): (refs 12, len >= 39), (13, >= 42), (14, >= 46), (15, >= 49); refs 16 crosses the floor_log2 boundary to 4 and needs len > 68. v_a1 (i carrying `sel`) reached 14/43 = 9767, three insns of live range short. Session 8 adds the reason the search space is narrow: refs are weighted by loop depth, so any reuse inside loop 2 explodes the numerator, and the live length can only be extended by placing the surviving use LATER in the post-loop stream.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate post-loop sites in the val==2 / val==5 arms that produce two JOINING definitions of an s32 whose last use sits later than v_a1's `sb $a0,%lo(D_800A37F8)` store - in particular a value defined in BOTH arms and consumed after the if/else join, which gives a much longer range than a def inside one arm. Generate one variant per site and read pri(pseudo 73) straight off tmp/grind/func_8003504C/s7/alloc.sh; only variants with pri < 9310 AND build_insns == 141 need a sandbox run. On h1 such a variant is a full match, since the swap is its only residual.

frontier.hypothesis: There is a fourth chassis class in which the p-walker's initialising copy is emitted at loop_start (satisfying INSN_LUID(s = p) > INSN_LUID(li 20)) while the pseudo still carries >= 10 weighted references - i.e. a loop.c-emitted copy whose destination is a SOURCE variable.
frontier.mechanism: Session 8 enumerated loop.c's loop_start emission points statically (move_movables 1652-1854, emit_iv_add_mult 5561/6098, check_dbra_loop 5868) but did not instrument them. combine_movables turns a movable that duplicates an earlier movable's value into a register COPY emitted at the LATER movable's insertion point - which is exactly the insn shape and exactly the position the requirement needs. Whether a copy of a call result into a source variable can ever be classified as such a movable is unresolved.
frontier.next_probe: Instrument tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c with a BB2-style env-gated hook at every emit_insn_before(loop_start)-class call site and print what each emits for func_8003504C on both chassis, paying particular attention to combine_movables' m->match copies and to move_movables' m->partial path. Then ask which class can emit `(set <source pseudo> <reg>)` after the constants. Any class that can is the win; use tmp/grind/func_8003504C/s8/solo8.sh to read the resulting .loop/.sched pre-loop region in one command.
